headline: High: Langflow’s default broad egress and unsandboxed server-side code can leak or corrupt shared flow data when paired with a non-runnable, read-only repo artifact.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Profile A is a non-runnable awesome-list with no I/O surfaces, so it cannot ingest B’s outputs by itself. Profile B can chain multiple agents and process uploaded files, but there is no documented shared channel or direct parser bridge from A to B. The only plausible pathway is manual copy/paste or file transfer, which is low blast radius.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies B-generated content into a Langflow node that treats it as instructions
IF A is converted into a runnable component or shared filesystem artifact
mitigations: Keep A as a static reference list, not an executable node.
Disable any flow step that ingests untrusted text as instructions.
Use explicit provenance labels on copied content.
Separate reference material from active flow inputs.

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches no data classes and has no egress, but B reads files, stores secrets, and has broad network egress to model providers and arbitrary HTTP services. In a shared workspace or uploaded-file flow, B can transmit intermediate outputs off-box by default. Because A is inert, the leakage risk is driven by B, but the pair still creates a default data-exposure pathway.
conditions: IF A is used as a source document inside a Langflow flow
IF B is configured with model providers or HTTP tools that receive uploaded file contents
mitigations: Avoid placing sensitive files in shared flow inputs.
Restrict B’s outbound HTTP/model-provider destinations.
Store secrets outside flow-visible components where possible.
Use a separate workspace for reference material and active flows.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no write or execution surface, so it cannot contend for resources. B can write the filesystem, execute shell commands, spawn subprocesses, and run unsandboxed Python code server-side. Even though B cannot modify git state, overlapping writes to shared files or server-side state can still race in default deployments; uncertainty about deployment isolation pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF B writes to a directory also used for uploaded files or shared server state
IF multiple Langflow instances operate on the same backend store
mitigations: Use per-flow isolated directories.
Disable concurrent writes to shared artifacts.
Run B in a container with a read-only base image where feasible.
Separate server state from uploaded-file storage.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A does not produce executable outputs, but B’s graph-based flows can chain multiple agents and wire tools into nodes. If A’s static content is imported into B as reference material, B may treat it as authoritative without verification. The pair therefore supports a default cascade from untrusted or stale reference content into downstream actions, though not enough for high severity because A is not an active generator.
conditions: IF A’s repository content is imported into a Langflow node as factual guidance
IF B forwards that content to an action-taking tool without validation
mitigations: Add a verification step before any action tool.
Mark A-derived content as non-authoritative.
Require human review for downstream side effects.
Use schema checks on any extracted facts.

E_compliance.rationale: No sensitive data class is documented for A, so there is no direct residency or regulated-data mismatch to cite for it. B does handle flow inputs, intermediate outputs, and stored secrets, but the profile does not specify a jurisdictional or certification conflict. The only supported conclusion is a low compliance risk from secret handling in B if operators place regulated data into flows.
conditions: IF regulated data is entered into B flows
IF B’s deployment lacks a documented retention or residency policy
mitigations: Do not place regulated data into flows without a policy review.
Document retention for flow inputs and intermediate outputs.
Keep secrets in a dedicated secret manager.
Review deployment residency before onboarding sensitive workloads.
